item.vignette: A 4-month-old boy has recurrent episodes of severe lactic acidosis and hypotonia. Enzyme assays show markedly reduced pyruvate dehydrogenase and 2-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase activities. Glycine concentration is normal. Immunoblotting shows markedly decreased lipoylation of the E2 subunits of both dehydrogenase complexes but preserved lipoylation of the H protein of the glycine cleavage system. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in LIPT1.
item.lead_in: Which biochemical process is most directly impaired?

options.A: Transfer of lipoyl groups to selected E2 subunits of mitochondrial 2-ketoacid dehydrogenase complexes
options.B: Insertion of sulfur atoms into protein-bound octanoyl groups by mitochondrial lipoic acid synthetase
options.C: Covalent attachment of biotin to mitochondrial carboxylases by holocarboxylase synthetase
options.D: Binding of thiamine pyrophosphate to the E1 subunit of pyruvate dehydrogenase
options.E: Transport of pyruvate from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix

item.tested_construct: LIPT1 is required for transfer of lipoic acid to selected 2-ketoacid dehydrogenase proteins, allowing their lipoylation and activation
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: LIPT1 deficiency causes a selective lipoic-acid transfer defect. The E2 subunits of pyruvate dehydrogenase and 2-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase require covalently attached lipoate for catalytic activity. In the original human LIPT1 disorder, lipoylation of these E2 proteins was markedly reduced while lipoylation of the glycine-cleavage H protein was preserved, distinguishing defective lipoate transfer to selected proteins from a generalized failure of lipoic-acid synthesis.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. LIPT1 is required for lipoylation and activation of selected 2-ketoacid dehydrogenases.
distractor_explanations.B: LIAS inserts sulfur into protein-bound octanoyl groups during mitochondrial lipoate biosynthesis; a generalized LIAS defect would not fit the preserved H-protein lipoylation described in the vignette.
distractor_explanations.C: Holocarboxylase synthetase attaches biotin to biotin-dependent carboxylases; it does not lipoylate the E2 subunits of PDH or 2-KGDH.
distractor_explanations.D: Thiamine pyrophosphate is a required E1 cofactor, but the demonstrated abnormality is loss of E2 lipoylation rather than impaired TPP binding.
distractor_explanations.E: Mitochondrial pyruvate transport occurs upstream of PDH and cannot explain simultaneous loss of PDH and 2-KGDH activity with selective E2 hypolipoylation.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize LIPT1 deficiency as a selective mitochondrial lipoate-transfer defect that reduces lipoylation and activity of 2-ketoacid dehydrogenase complexes.

item.vignette: A 5-year-old girl has nonprogressive cerebellar ataxia, short stature, and mild intellectual disability. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in PMPCA. Patient fibroblasts accumulate precursor forms of several nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins, including incompletely processed frataxin, despite normal delivery of these proteins into mitochondria.
item.lead_in: Which cellular process is most directly impaired?

options.A: Recognition of mitochondrial targeting sequences by TOM20 at the outer mitochondrial membrane
options.B: Proteolytic maturation of imported mitochondrial precursor proteins by the mitochondrial processing peptidase
options.C: TIM22-dependent insertion of multipass carrier proteins into the inner mitochondrial membrane
options.D: Replication of mitochondrial DNA by DNA polymerase gamma
options.E: Post-transcriptional polyadenylation of mitochondrial messenger RNAs

item.tested_construct: PMPCA encodes the alpha subunit of mitochondrial processing peptidase, which is required for maturation of many imported nuclear-encoded mitochondrial precursor proteins
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Most nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins are synthesized as precursor proteins carrying targeting presequences. After mitochondrial import, the mitochondrial processing peptidase removes targeting sequences to generate mature proteins. PMPCA encodes the alpha subunit of this processing complex; pathogenic variants impair precursor maturation, including processing of frataxin.

distractor_explanations.A: TOM20 participates in initial recognition of many mitochondrial targeting sequences, but the vignette states that import occurs and precursor proteins accumulate after entry.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. PMPCA dysfunction impairs mitochondrial processing peptidase activity and therefore maturation of imported precursor proteins.
distractor_explanations.C: TIM22 inserts a restricted class of multipass inner-membrane carriers; PMPCA deficiency instead causes defective proteolytic maturation of many imported precursor proteins.
distractor_explanations.D: POLG replicates mitochondrial DNA and does not cleave targeting presequences from nuclear-encoded proteins.
distractor_explanations.E: Mitochondrial mRNA polyadenylation is a post-transcriptional RNA process and cannot explain accumulation of unprocessed imported protein precursors.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish mitochondrial protein import from post-import processing: PMPCA deficiency impairs mitochondrial processing peptidase-mediated maturation of nuclear-encoded precursor proteins.

item.vignette: A 6-year-old boy has recurrent bacterial and viral infections, severe eczema, skeletal dysplasia, and developmental delay. Laboratory studies show lymphopenia and reduced intracellular UDP-N-acetylglucosamine. Genetic testing identifies biallelic hypomorphic variants in PGM3, and patient cells show reduced N-linked and O-linked protein glycosylation.
item.lead_in: Which metabolic reaction is most directly impaired?

options.A: Conversion of fructose-6-phosphate and glutamine to glucosamine-6-phosphate
options.D: Formation of UDP-N-acetylglucosamine from N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate and UTP
options.E: Conversion of UDP-N-acetylglucosamine to N-acetylmannosamine and UDP by GNE

item.tested_construct: PGM3 converts N-acetylglucosamine-6-phosphate to N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate during UDP-GlcNAc synthesis
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: PGM3 is a phosphoacetylglucosamine mutase in the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway. It converts GlcNAc-6-phosphate to GlcNAc-1-phosphate, which is subsequently used to generate UDP-GlcNAc. UDP-GlcNAc supplies multiple glycosylation pathways, explaining the combined immune, skeletal, and neurologic phenotype when PGM3 activity is reduced.

distractor_explanations.A: GFPT catalyzes the upstream formation of glucosamine-6-phosphate from fructose-6-phosphate and glutamine; this is not the PGM3 reaction.
distractor_explanations.B: GNPNAT1 catalyzes acetylation of glucosamine-6-phosphate upstream of PGM3.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. PGM3 interconverts GlcNAc-6-phosphate and GlcNAc-1-phosphate, supplying substrate for UDP-GlcNAc synthesis.
distractor_explanations.D: UAP1 catalyzes the downstream uridylation step that forms UDP-GlcNAc from GlcNAc-1-phosphate and UTP.
distractor_explanations.E: GNE converts UDP-GlcNAc to N-acetylmannosamine and UDP at the entry to sialic-acid biosynthesis; it is downstream of UDP-GlcNAc production and is not the PGM3 reaction.

explanation.educational_objective: Link PGM3 immunodeficiency to impaired GlcNAc-6-phosphate to GlcNAc-1-phosphate conversion and reduced UDP-GlcNAc availability for protein glycosylation.

item.vignette: A 2-year-old boy from a French-Canadian founder population has developmental delay and recurrent episodes of severe lactic acidosis during minor illnesses. Muscle studies show a marked cytochrome c oxidase deficiency. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in LRPPRC. Mitochondrial DNA copy number is normal, but steady-state levels of multiple mitochondrial messenger RNAs are markedly reduced.
item.lead_in: Which molecular process is most directly impaired?

options.A: Replication of mitochondrial DNA by DNA polymerase gamma
options.B: Initiation of mitochondrial transcription by the POLRMT-TFAM machinery
options.C: Cleavage of polycistronic mitochondrial transcripts at transfer-RNA boundaries
options.D: Post-transcriptional stabilization and polyadenylation of mitochondrial messenger RNAs
options.E: Aminoacylation of mitochondrial transfer RNAs before translation

item.tested_construct: LRPPRC forms an RNA-binding complex that stabilizes mitochondrial mRNAs and supports their polyadenylation and coordinated translation
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: LRPPRC acts at the post-transcriptional level in mitochondria. In complex with RNA-binding partners such as SLIRP, it helps maintain mitochondrial mRNA stability and polyadenylation and coordinates translation. LRPPRC deficiency therefore lowers steady-state mitochondrial mRNA levels despite preserved mitochondrial DNA copy number.

distractor_explanations.A: POLG-dependent mtDNA replication failure would reduce or deplete mitochondrial DNA itself; copy number is normal in this vignette.
distractor_explanations.B: POLRMT and TFAM are central to mitochondrial transcription initiation, but LRPPRC primarily regulates mitochondrial RNA after transcription.
distractor_explanations.C: Mitochondrial transcript cleavage is performed by RNA-processing machinery at tRNA junctions and is not the principal LRPPRC function.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. LRPPRC loss destabilizes mitochondrial mRNAs and impairs their polyadenylation and coordinated translation.
distractor_explanations.E: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases charge mitochondrial tRNAs; failure of that process does not directly explain selective loss of steady-state mitochondrial mRNAs.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize LRPPRC deficiency as a post-transcriptional mitochondrial gene-expression defect involving mRNA stabilization, polyadenylation, and coordinated translation.

item.vignette: A 10-year-old boy has progressive dystonia, gait difficulty, polycythemia, and chronic liver disease. Whole-blood manganese concentration is markedly elevated, and T1-weighted brain MRI shows symmetric hyperintensity of the basal ganglia. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC30A10.
item.lead_in: Which transport function is most directly impaired?

options.A: Cellular manganese uptake mediated by SLC39A8
options.B: Manganese uptake into hepatocytes mediated by SLC39A14
options.C: Canalicular copper export mediated by ATP7B
options.D: Cellular iron export mediated by ferroportin
options.E: Cell-surface manganese efflux mediated by SLC30A10

item.tested_construct: SLC30A10 is a cell-surface manganese efflux transporter; loss of trafficking or efflux function causes cellular and systemic manganese accumulation
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: SLC30A10 localizes to the cell surface and exports manganese, protecting cells from manganese toxicity. Disease-causing variants can prevent appropriate surface trafficking or directly impair efflux, producing hypermanganesemia with dystonia, polycythemia, and liver disease.

distractor_explanations.A: SLC39A8 promotes manganese uptake and its deficiency causes systemic manganese deficiency with glycosylation abnormalities, the opposite metal phenotype.
distractor_explanations.B: SLC39A14 is a manganese influx transporter important for tissue uptake; its deficiency can also cause manganese neurotoxicity but is mechanistically distinct from SLC30A10 loss.
distractor_explanations.C: ATP7B exports copper into bile; its failure causes copper accumulation rather than isolated hypermanganesemia.
distractor_explanations.D: Ferroportin exports iron and does not account for the characteristic manganese accumulation and SLC30A10 genotype.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. SLC30A10 mediates cell-surface manganese efflux, and loss of this function increases cellular manganese burden.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize SLC30A10-associated hypermanganesemia as failure of cell-surface manganese efflux rather than a defect in copper, iron, or manganese-uptake pathways.
